paragraphs: Optimal transport can describe how a probability distribution changes over time. Different choices about the cost of motion and the cost of intermediate distributions produce different versions of this problem. The paper brings these variations into one computational framework, including Schrödinger bridges, unbalanced transport, and transport subject to physical constraints.

The central difficulty is that the best path of distributions is unknown and can be expensive to compute. The authors develop a deep learning approach based on a dual formulation of the underlying optimization problems. Their method does not require simulating the learned trajectories or propagating training derivatives through them. It also avoids requiring optimal couplings, the correspondences that specify how probability mass should be transported.

The framework is demonstrated on single-cell trajectory inference, where prior knowledge about the dynamics matters for correct predictions. The authors report better performance than previous approaches in that application. The contribution combines a common treatment of several transport problems with a computational strategy that removes specific trajectory-related requirements.
icml-2024-a-computational-framework-for-.tldr: A unified deep learning framework solves several optimal transport problems without simulating learned trajectories or needing optimal couplings.

paragraphs: A mixture-of-experts classifier combines several predictive models using a gate that determines their contributions. Although related regression models had received theoretical attention, the paper addresses a gap for classification: how quickly maximum likelihood estimation recovers the predictive distribution and model parameters as the amount of data increases.

The authors establish convergence rates for mixtures with softmax gating and multinomial logistic experts. They identify a problematic case in which some expert parameters vanish. In that setting, interactions between the gating function and expert functions can produce convergence slower than polynomial rates. These interactions are expressed through partial differential equations, connecting the statistical difficulty to the mathematical structure of the model.

To address this behavior, the paper introduces a class of modified softmax gates that transform inputs before applying the gating functions. The modification removes the identified interaction and substantially improves parameter estimation rates. The result explains a specific source of slow estimation and shows how changing the gate can improve the theoretical behavior of this classification model.
icml-2024-a-general-theory-for-softmax-g.tldr: The paper identifies slow estimation in softmax-gated classification mixtures and introduces modified gates that improve parameter convergence rates.

paragraphs: The lifted multicut problem appears in several computer vision applications. Exact solution methods based on linear programming depend on understanding the geometry of its feasible solutions, represented by a polytope. Facets are the boundary faces of greatest dimension, making it useful to distinguish inequalities that define facets from inequalities that do not.

The paper resolves this question for lower box inequalities. It establishes conditions that are both necessary and sufficient, so they characterize exactly when an inequality of this type defines a facet. Those conditions are also efficiently decidable. This combination provides a complete mathematical characterization together with a practical way to check whether the characterization applies.

For cut inequalities, the authors establish a different kind of result: deciding whether an inequality defines a facet is NP-hard. This identifies a computational obstacle to obtaining a general efficient decision procedure for that family. Together, the two findings complete the analysis of canonical facets described in the paper and clarify which geometric questions admit efficient checks.
icml-2024-box-facets-and-cut-facets-of-l.tldr: Lower box facets receive an efficiently checkable exact characterization, while recognizing cut facets is shown to be NP-hard.

paragraphs: Gaussian process factor analysis seeks smooth, low-dimensional patterns underlying recordings from many neurons. Treating neural firing rates as Gaussian observations makes inference tractable, but directly modeling spike counts creates a harder mathematical problem. The likelihood no longer combines conveniently with the rest of the model, prompting earlier approaches to use numerical integration, approximations, or black-box inference.

The proposed ccGPFA method changes this computational situation through data augmentation. It introduces auxiliary quantities that make the model conditionally conjugate: once those quantities are included, the relevant inference updates take an analytically convenient form. This enables closed-form updates within a variational expectation-maximization algorithm while retaining a model for spike count observations.

The same structure supports further computational improvements. The authors show how to use sparse Gaussian processes for scaling and natural gradients to accelerate inference. They also report experiments demonstrating the method's efficacy. The contribution is a count-data formulation whose mathematical structure directly supports simpler inference, scalable computation, and recovery of latent neural activity trajectories.
icml-2024-conditionally-conjugate-gaussi.tldr: ccGPFA uses data augmentation to make latent trajectory inference from neural spike counts analytically and computationally tractable.

paragraphs: Saddle-point optimization involves minimizing a function in some variables while maximizing it in others. This paper studies stochastic first-order methods for convex-concave problems, where updates use noisy gradient information. A central difficulty is that gradients can become arbitrarily large as optimization proceeds, causing unstable updates or even divergence.

The authors propose a regularization technique that stabilizes the sequence of iterates. Their analysis provides performance guarantees in settings that allow an unbounded domain and gradient noise that grows linearly with the size of the iterates. This matters because the analysis accommodates potentially increasing noise instead of depending on a fixed bound that may fail during optimization.

The paper also applies the method to reinforcement learning with an average-reward Markov decision process. In that setting, it provides guarantees for finding nearly optimal policies without advance knowledge of the bias span. The contribution therefore includes both general optimization results and a concrete learning application in which the method removes a prior-knowledge requirement.
icml-2024-dealing-with-unbounded-gradien.tldr: A regularization method stabilizes stochastic saddle-point optimization with potentially unbounded gradients and supports average-reward reinforcement learning guarantees.

paragraphs: Density ratio estimation measures how the probability of an observation differs between a reference distribution and a target distribution. Outliers can distort that comparison. This paper develops two estimators designed to remain robust even when both distributions contain heavy contamination, a property the authors call doubly strong robustness.

Both methods use divergences with a weighting function that reduces the adverse influence of outliers. The first, Weighted DRE, is based on unnormalized Kullback-Leibler divergence and leads to a convex optimization problem. The second, gamma-DRE, uses gamma-divergence to improve a problem involving Weighted DRE's normalizing term. Its optimization instead takes the form of a difference of convex functions and requires more computation.

The methods therefore offer different computational tradeoffs within the same robustness objective. Numerical experiments show greater robustness than previous approaches. The key finding concerns contamination on both sides of the ratio: the methods address settings where neither the reference data nor the target data can be treated as free of substantial outlier effects.
icml-2024-density-ratio-estimation-with-.tldr: Two weighted density ratio estimators improve robustness to heavy contamination in both reference and target distributions, with different computational costs.

paragraphs: A generative model may need to respect constraints beyond resembling its training examples. This paper studies a setting where additional information comes from an oracle that can identify samples outside the support of the true data distribution. Such an oracle supplies negative information about which outputs should fall outside the intended set of possibilities.

The authors introduce Gen-neG, a denoising diffusion approach that incorporates this information during model learning. It builds on classifier guidance to steer generation toward the positive support region indicated by the oracle. The approach connects an external judgment about unacceptable samples to the process that progressively constructs a generated sample.

Experiments demonstrate the method's utility for collision avoidance in self-driving simulators and safety-guarded human motion generation. These results support the usefulness of oracle information in the evaluated constrained generation settings. The contribution depends on having the stated source of side information: a mechanism that can label samples as outside the target distribution's support, in addition to the training dataset.
icml-2024-dont-be-so-negative-score-base.tldr: Gen-neG uses an oracle's negative labels to guide diffusion generation toward the intended support of a constrained data distribution.

paragraphs: Language models store key and value representations of past tokens so they can reuse them during generation. This cache grows with sequence length and batch size, creating a memory burden. Dynamic Memory Compression addresses that burden by compressing the cache online while the model generates text.

The model learns different compression ratios for different attention heads and layers. Existing pretrained models are adapted through continued pretraining on a very small fraction of the original data, without adding parameters. The authors retrofit Llama 2 models with 7, 13, and 70 billion parameters, demonstrating that the approach can be applied to already trained language models.

The reported results include up to approximately 3.7 times greater autoregressive throughput on an NVIDIA H100 and preserved downstream performance with up to fourfold cache compression. DMC outperforms the evaluated adapted grouped-query attention and cache eviction approaches. It can also be combined with grouped-query attention for additional gains. Reducing cache size makes room for longer contexts and larger batches within a given memory budget.
icml-2024-dynamic-memory-compression-ret.tldr: DMC teaches pretrained language models to compress their attention caches adaptively, preserving tested performance with up to fourfold compression.

paragraphs: Deep networks can represent equivalent computations with differently ordered internal units. These permutation symmetries complicate operations such as comparing models or merging their weights, because corresponding parts may occupy different positions. Finding the optimal alignment is NP-hard, and earlier relaxed approaches can be slow or produce suboptimal matches.

Deep-Align learns to perform weight alignment. The authors first prove that the alignment problem follows two fundamental symmetries, then design a neural architecture that respects them. The framework requires no labeled data. Its structure therefore incorporates mathematical properties of the task while learning how to produce useful permutations.

Across several network architectures and learning settings, a single feed-forward pass produces alignments that are better than or equivalent to those from the evaluated optimization algorithms. The resulting alignments also serve as effective starting points for other methods, improving solutions and substantially accelerating convergence. These empirical findings support Deep-Align as both a direct alignment method and an initialization strategy, without implying that it solves every instance optimally.
icml-2024-equivariant-deep-weight-space-.tldr: Deep-Align learns symmetry-respecting weight alignments without labeled data and produces strong alignments in a single feed-forward pass.

paragraphs: Dense-to-sparse mixture-of-experts models use temperature to control how broadly a softmax gate distributes weight across experts. This allows the degree of sparsity to change during training instead of fixing the number of active experts. The paper investigates what this design means for maximum likelihood parameter estimation in Gaussian mixtures of experts.

The analysis identifies interactions between temperature and other parameters, expressed through partial differential equations. Because of these interactions, parameter estimates can converge more slowly than any polynomial rate, potentially as slowly as one divided by the logarithm of the sample size. The finding concerns statistical estimation as data increases, highlighting a difficulty behind the gate's apparent flexibility.

The authors propose inserting an activation function between the gate's linear layer and its softmax. Under linear independence conditions on that activation function and its derivatives, they establish improved polynomial parameter estimation rates. A simulation study supports the theoretical results. The improvement is thus tied to a specific architectural modification and stated mathematical conditions on the chosen activation.
icml-2024-is-temperature-sample-efficien.tldr: Temperature-based Gaussian expert gating can yield extremely slow parameter estimation, while a suitably chosen activation restores polynomial convergence rates.

paragraphs: Cooperating reinforcement learning agents may share a clear objective while struggling to discover a sequence of actions that reaches it. In complex tasks, learning these paths can take considerable time, and trained agents may still fail to find them. LAGMA addresses this difficulty by giving learning agents a reference path toward the goal.

The reference path is constructed in a learned latent space, a compact representation of the task. A modified vector-quantized variational autoencoder builds a quantized space to support efficient use of samples. An extended codebook then generates goal-reaching trajectories within that space. Finally, an intrinsic reward encourages transitions toward a sampled trajectory, providing an additional training incentive linked to progress along the reference path.

The authors evaluate LAGMA in StarCraft II with both dense and sparse rewards, as well as Google Research Football. They report improved performance over state-of-the-art baselines in these experiments. The findings support combining a compact learned representation, goal-path generation, and internal reward guidance to help teams learn how to reach shared objectives.
icml-2024-lagma-latent-goal-guided-multi.tldr: LAGMA guides cooperating agents with goal-reaching paths in a learned latent space and rewards progress toward those paths.

paragraphs: This paper represents learning as inference in a Gaussian factor graph. Inputs, outputs, parameters, and intermediate activations are all treated as random variables within one graphical model. Training and prediction become related inference problems, distinguished by which quantities are observed and which must be inferred.

The authors use belief propagation to solve these problems, and their experiments show that it can do so efficiently. Its updates are local, meaning computation proceeds through interactions within the graph. That locality creates opportunities for distributed and asynchronous training. The approach also scales to deep networks, extending the graphical formulation beyond shallow models.

Continual learning follows naturally from the probabilistic representation: the estimated posterior after one task becomes the prior for the next. In video denoising, the authors demonstrate benefits from learnable parameters compared with a classical factor graph approach. They also report encouraging continual image classification results. Together, these experiments support the framework's ability to combine deep learning, local inference, and transfer of learned uncertainty between successive tasks.
icml-2024-learning-in-deep-factor-graphs.tldr: Deep Gaussian factor graphs unify training and prediction as local belief-propagation inference and carry learned posteriors between tasks.

paragraphs: A model's confidence should reflect whether alternative labels remain plausible given its training data. Predictive normalized maximum likelihood, or pNML, approaches uncertainty by considering every possible label for a test point. When several labels remain consistent with the model and data, the resulting prediction becomes less confident.

The paper introduces IF-COMP as a scalable, efficient approximation to this distribution. It linearizes the model using a temperature-scaled Boltzmann influence function. This provides a computational route to the pNML approach while supporting both calibrated predictions and measurements of data complexity. The complexity measurements apply in settings with labels and in settings without them.

The authors evaluate IF-COMP on uncertainty calibration, detecting incorrect labels, and identifying out-of-distribution data. Across these experiments, it consistently matches or exceeds strong baseline methods. The results connect one approximation method to several reliability tasks: assessing prediction confidence, finding questionable annotations, and recognizing unfamiliar inputs. Its significance lies in making a label-alternative view of uncertainty usable at greater computational scale.
icml-2024-measuring-stochastic-data-comp.tldr: IF-COMP efficiently approximates a distribution that considers alternative labels, supporting uncertainty calibration, mislabel detection, and out-of-distribution detection.

paragraphs: This paper examines how the hardware used for machine learning can affect both model performance and fairness across demographic groups. Hardware is often treated as a practical infrastructure choice, while algorithms and data receive more attention. The authors show that hardware choices can worsen existing disparities, making hardware selection relevant to assessing how evenly a model serves different groups.

The investigation combines theoretical reasoning with empirical analysis. The authors attribute the discrepancies to variations in gradient flows and loss surfaces across demographic groups. These concepts describe how learning updates move a model’s parameters and how its error changes as those parameters vary. This connects hardware-related performance imbalances to the behavior of model optimization.

The paper also proposes a strategy reported to mitigate these imbalances effectively. Its findings are especially relevant to machine-learning services where users may have little control over deployment hardware. The broader implication is that understanding a model’s fairness can require attention to the hardware on which it operates, alongside its algorithms and data.
icml-2024-on-the-fairness-impacts-of-har.tldr: Hardware choices can worsen performance disparities across demographic groups, and this paper investigates why and proposes a strategy to mitigate them.

paragraphs: Recent off-policy reinforcement learning methods have improved sample efficiency partly by using regularization to support more gradient updates. However, testing individual techniques in narrow settings makes it difficult to determine which mechanisms explain those improvements. This paper examines established regularization choices within a broader comparison of agents and tasks.

The authors implement more than 60 agents and test them on 14 tasks drawn from two simulation benchmarks. They track training measurements related to overestimated values, overfitting, and loss of plasticity, or the ability to keep learning. These measurements connect the comparison to the problems that motivate the regularizers, alongside evaluating the resulting policies.

The effectiveness of a particular setup varies by task, but some combinations show consistently strong and robust performance across the evaluation. A suitably regularized Soft Actor-Critic agent reliably finds a better-performing policy within the studied training regime, a result previously associated mainly with model-based approaches. The findings emphasize the importance of regularization combinations when interpreting progress in sample-efficient reinforcement learning.
icml-2024-overestimation-overfitting-and.tldr: A broad comparison finds that effective regularization combinations can make a simple Soft Actor-Critic agent highly competitive within the tested training regime.

paragraphs: Estimating an individual treatment effect means predicting how a person's outcome would change under a different treatment. Observational data presents a fundamental obstacle: each person has an observed outcome under only the treatment they received. Methods that fill this gap with inferred pseudo-outcomes depend on how accurately those missing outcomes are estimated.

PairNet introduces a training strategy based on pairs of examples and their factual, observed outcomes. It minimizes losses defined over these pairs, using observed information to train treatment-effect estimates. The strategy is model-agnostic and described as easy to implement, so its contribution is a training approach that can be used with different underlying models.

For binary treatments, the theoretical analysis establishes consistency as an estimator of treatment-effect risk and smaller generalization error than baseline models. Experiments compare PairNet with thirteen existing methods across eight benchmarks, including discrete and continuous treatments, and report significantly lower treatment-effect error. The theoretical result specifically concerns binary treatment, while the empirical evaluation covers a broader range of treatment settings.
icml-2024-pairnet-training-with-observed.tldr: PairNet trains treatment-effect models using pairs of observed outcomes and reports lower estimation error across discrete and continuous treatment benchmarks.

paragraphs: Rapidly changing physical systems are difficult for learned simulators, especially when motion transports sharp boundaries or produces steep spatial gradients. Their behavior can involve large nonlinear systems of partial differential equations and additional constitutive models. This paper extends a physics-aware neural architecture to better represent these demanding forms of evolution.

The starting point is PARC, which uses a differentiator-integrator architecture to model change over space and time. PARCv2 adds differential operators for advection-reaction-diffusion equations and a hybrid integral solver intended to support stable predictions over long periods. These architectural choices encode structure associated with physical evolution into the model's computation.

The authors test PARCv2 on Burgers and Navier-Stokes fluid dynamics problems, then apply it to more complex shock-induced reactions in energetic materials. They compare its behavior with other physics-informed and learning-bias models. The results demonstrate its potential for unsteady and advection-dominated dynamics. The contribution is an extension of the architecture's physical modeling capabilities, supported by evaluations spanning standard equations and a more complex application.
icml-2024-parcv2-physics-aware-recurrent.tldr: PARCv2 adds physical differential operators and a hybrid integrator to model rapidly changing, advection-dominated systems.

paragraphs: Vision-language models can reason about images, but spatial tasks often require coordinates, actions, or trajectories rather than a textual response. PIVOT connects these output requirements through visual prompting, without fine-tuning on task-specific data. It turns the search for a spatial answer into a sequence of visual questions.

At each iteration, an image is annotated with candidate actions, locations, or trajectories that the model can identify and compare. The model chooses the most promising proposals, and those proposals are refined for the next round. Repeating this process lets textual selections guide a search over the continuous outputs needed by a robot or another spatial system.

The authors investigate real-world navigation and manipulation, simulated instruction following, and spatial inference tasks including localization. They demonstrate zero-shot robotic control without robot training data and navigation across varied environments. Performance remains far from perfect, as the authors explicitly acknowledge. The findings nevertheless show that iterative visual choices can draw actionable spatial knowledge from existing large vision-language models.
icml-2024-pivot-iterative-visual-prompti.tldr: PIVOT repeatedly asks vision-language models to select and refine visual proposals, enabling spatial reasoning and zero-shot robotic control.

paragraphs: Experimental design methods choose which candidates to investigate next, but they can concentrate too heavily on already promising regions. This favors exploitation over exploration and can trap the search around local optima. The resulting collection may contain good individual candidates while failing to cover a diverse range of useful discoveries.

The paper extends Vendi scores, which measure diversity through similarities between items, to incorporate quality. These quality-weighted scores provide a way to judge collections using both how good their members are and how varied they are. The authors use them to construct experimental design policies with a flexible balance between quality and diversity.

Applications include drug discovery, materials discovery, and reinforcement learning. The reported algorithms assemble diverse sets of high-performing points and increase the number of effective discoveries by 70% to 170% compared with baselines. These results support evaluating the quality and diversity of a collection together when directing search. The reported gains concern effective discoveries in the evaluated applications, rather than a universal improvement for every search problem.
icml-2024-quality-weighted-vendi-scores-.tldr: Quality-weighted Vendi scores balance candidate quality and diversity, increasing effective discoveries by 70%–170% over evaluated baselines.

paragraphs: Discovering causal structure becomes harder when some relevant variables are unobserved and may themselves be causally connected. Existing constraint-based approaches use tests such as conditional independence or rank deficiency, but can encounter testing-order effects, propagated errors, and difficult significance choices. The paper develops score-based alternatives for this latent-variable setting.

The authors show that an appropriately formulated scoring function can achieve score equivalence and consistency for learning latent causal structures. They also establish identifiability guarantees for structures containing causally related hidden variables. These results provide a theoretical basis for comparing candidate structures through a score rather than relying solely on sequences of individual constraint tests.

To construct the methods, the paper characterizes degrees of freedom in the distribution over observed variables under several structural assumptions from the literature. This supports both exact and continuous score-based methods and connects existing approaches within a common perspective. Experiments validate their effectiveness. The guarantees remain associated with the structural settings analyzed, making those assumptions central to interpreting what hidden causal structure can be recovered.
icml-2024-score-based-causal-discovery-o.tldr: The paper develops score-based methods with theoretical guarantees for discovering causal structures containing causally related latent variables.

paragraphs: Voice conversion changes speaker characteristics while retaining linguistic content. Many approaches try to explicitly separate these attributes in their representations, but task-specific separation losses can discard information. SelfVC instead trains a controllable conversion model using entangled representations obtained from self-supervised speech learning and speaker verification models.

The framework extracts prosodic information from the audio signal and self-supervised representations to train predictive components within the synthesis model. It then improves that model iteratively using examples the model synthesizes itself. These examples create a challenging training objective, making the model's own generated speech part of the process for improving subsequent conversion.

The authors find that adding self-synthesized examples improves generated speaker similarity compared with a baseline trained only on heuristically perturbed inputs. The framework uses no text during training and reports state-of-the-art zero-shot conversion results on naturalness, speaker similarity, and intelligibility. The contribution combines controllable synthesis from entangled representations with a training strategy that reuses generated examples to improve voice conversion.
icml-2024-selfvc-voice-conversion-with-i.tldr: SelfVC improves text-free voice conversion through iterative training on self-synthesized examples while using entangled speech representations.

paragraphs: Information-theoretic generalization bounds relate performance on unseen data to dependence between training data and the learned model. Their practical use in deep learning is limited by the difficulty of measuring mutual information in high dimensions. This paper studies slicing: training within randomly selected, lower-dimensional subspaces of parameter space.

The authors derive tighter bounds tailored to sliced training, using disintegrated mutual information and k-sliced mutual information as more scalable dependence measures. Their analysis demonstrates improved generalization through slicing. They then extend the framework to models whose parameters do not lie exactly within random subspaces, using rate-distortion theory to account for the discrepancy.

That extension introduces a distortion term measuring how compressible a model is under slicing. It tightens existing bounds without requiring the model to be compressed or sacrificing performance. The authors also propose regularization that lets practitioners influence generalization through compressibility. Experiments validate the results and produce non-vacuous information-theoretic bounds for neural networks, meaning bounds informative enough to provide a substantive guarantee.
icml-2024-slicing-mutual-information-gen.tldr: Slicing parameter space yields more tractable generalization bounds, with an extension that connects neural-network compressibility to informative guarantees.

paragraphs: Neural Walk-on-Spheres is a neural solver for high-dimensional Poisson equations. These equations specify a mathematical relationship that the learned solution must satisfy across a domain. The method builds its training losses from stochastic representations and recursive solutions on spheres contained within that domain.

This construction gives the solver two useful computational properties: it is highly parallelizable, and evaluating its loss does not require spatial gradients. The paper compares the method with physics-informed neural networks, the Deep Ritz method, and approaches based on stochastic differential equations. The comparison examines accuracy alongside speed and computational cost, rather than assessing solution quality alone.

Across several challenging high-dimensional numerical examples, the authors report better performance on these criteria. Relative to commonly used physics-informed neural networks, NWoS can reduce memory usage and errors by orders of magnitude. They also apply it to PDE-constrained optimization and molecular dynamics. These results show how the sphere-based formulation can support efficient neural equation solving in both numerical tests and the practical applications examined.
icml-2024-solving-poisson-equations-usin.tldr: Neural Walk-on-Spheres solves high-dimensional Poisson equations using parallelizable losses that avoid spatial gradients and show substantial computational gains.

paragraphs: Differentiable causal discovery searches for a directed acyclic graph by treating graph learning as continuous optimization. A central requirement is preventing directed cycles. Existing approaches can become numerically unstable and perform poorly beyond a few dozen variables, limiting the scale at which this strategy is useful.

Stable Differentiable Causal Discovery changes both the acyclicity constraint and the training procedure. Its alternative constraint is fast to compute and more stable in theoretical analysis and experiments. The training procedure is designed for sparse causal graphs, where relatively few connections are present. The authors derive the method and prove its stability and correctness.

Evaluation includes observational and interventional data at both small and large scales. SDCD achieves faster convergence and greater accuracy than the methods compared, and scales to thousands of variables. The findings connect an improved mathematical constraint with a training strategy suited to sparse structure. Together, these changes address the numerical difficulty that has restricted the practical scale of continuous causal graph learning.
icml-2024-stable-differentiable-causal-d.tldr: SDCD combines a more stable acyclicity constraint with sparse-graph training to scale differentiable causal discovery to thousands of variables.

paragraphs: Time series often come with context that helps explain their patterns, such as location or changing weather. Generating useful synthetic sequences requires accounting for that context, but metadata can combine categories, numerical values, and variables that change over time. TIME WEAVER is a diffusion model designed to use this heterogeneous information.

The paper also addresses how conditional generation should be evaluated. A generated sequence may look realistic while failing to reflect the metadata it was given. The authors show that straightforward adaptations of image-generation metrics do not adequately penalize this failure. They introduce an evaluation metric that captures both realism and specificity to the conditioning information.

Experiments cover real-world energy, medical, air quality, and traffic datasets. TIME WEAVER outperforms state-of-the-art benchmarks, including generative adversarial networks, by up to 30% in downstream classification tasks. That reported improvement concerns the evaluated downstream tasks. The broader contribution pairs a model for varied contextual inputs with an evaluation method that checks whether generated sequences actually express their requested context.
icml-2024-time-weaver-a-conditional-time.tldr: TIME WEAVER generates time series from heterogeneous metadata and introduces an evaluation metric for realism and contextual specificity.
